item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
As interesting as it is, this article breaks the immersion royally, mostly because of tone. I cannot feel as it being a technical document, the constant concern about it being theft by hostiles seems out of place, the direct prohibition of housing it at a Foundation facility is silly, I'm left with all the questions about details that an SCP actually should answer, like how fast is this thing? At what rate the radius increase? What is the rate of decay of materials and people next to it?

The piece is good, but not good enough to overlook so many egregious problems with the format. It is old, but the problems are not of the kind that weren't problems at the time. I see no reason to accept it as it is, and I personally do not.

Revised containment proposal: an underground facility, purposefully dug to be unstable.

That way, if this ever does activate again, the first thing dissolved would be the supports holding up the roof. Since it isn't particularly durable the resulting collapse would stop the device before the effect spreads.

item.title: Re: why?

In the SCP-verse, there are groups with technology well in advance of "real" modern tech. The Foundation is one of these groups.

They could make things which don't make sense. Not that they necessarily understand how these things function in terms of science.

I like this SCP, but there's a lot about it that I'm anxious to see clarified, as far as the functioning of the device goes. Was this thing really built solely by humans? If so, how did they come up with the tech. to obliterate humans and synthetic objects without affecting anything else?

Frankly, I think t hat would be way too hard an angle to make in a compelling way, because science like the one displayed by the globe is far beyond what people should be capable of. I think it would be interesting if this ostensibly human endeavor had the aid of something supernatural with an agenda of its own, just an idea though.
